newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta index hits new record on active buying.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta index hits new record on active buying.

text.p: Sustained buying interest almost across the board pushed the Jakarta index to a record high of 712.61 points on Wednesday, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 11.30 points, or 1.61 percent, to close at 712.61 points, breaking its previous best of 710.43 points recorded on February 14.
Gainers led losers by 95 to 45, with 55 counters unchanged. Total turnover was 641.3 billion rupiah on a volume of 289.3 million shares.
Brokers said since late in the morning session many foreign buyers had re-entered the market, which previously had been dominated by local players, pushing the index up.

Blue-chips such as telecommunications firm Telkom, cigarette makers Gudang Garam and Sampoerna as well as cement maker Semen Gresik were among the target of foreign buyers, causing the sharp rise in the index, brokers said.
The four firms have a weight of 36.34 percent on the index.
Telkom closed 75 rupiah higher at 4,175 rupiah on a volume of about six million shares, while Semen Gresik rose 250 rupiah to 7,400 rupiah on 1.1 million shares.
Gudang Garam rose 5.50 percent to 11,500 rupiah on 498,000 shares, while its competitor Sampoerna rose 2.32 percent to 14,350 rupiah on 264,000 shares.
Local-investors bought actively on counters which have been subject to rumours of rights issues, take-overs and acquisitions such as Barito Pacific, Asahimas, Multipolar and Hero.
Timber firm Barito Pacific was the most active stock with 21.2 million shares traded, rising 225 rupiah on 2,300 rupiah on market talk of possible entry of business tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
One broker with Singaporean firm said he had heard Barito shares would be managed to touch a price of 3,000 rupiah.
"From our side, its not really a matter of who is going to control the company. We are just looking for short-term profit," he added.

Glass maker Asahimas was also active, rising 200 rupiah to 1,650 rupiah on a turnover of 15.9 million shares on the expectation of higher 1997 earnings. Brokers said it was also due to market talk of a possible rights issue.
